verdicts.observation: Uneven green shoots and a dark rooted base still read as a small grass tuft at 2x.
Separated upper shoots and the broader green base preserve the grass-tuft reading at 2x.
The low horizontal cluster retains short green blades and reads as a squat grass patch at 2x.
Pale seed heads above a narrow green stem cluster retain the tall grass identity at 2x.
Two white heads with warm centers remain distinct above green foliage, including at 2x.
Yellow heads remain distinguishable from the lower green foliage and read as a tiny flower cluster at 2x.
The source has clear purple petals; the fitted heads become isolated pale and orange marks with too little purple to read as purple flowers at 2x.
Bright red flower heads above a green base preserve the red-flower reading at 2x despite simplified stems.
The broad brown cap and pale descending stalk remain recognizable as a mushroom at 2x.
The red cap, pale cap marks, and light stalk preserve the spotted-mushroom identity at 2x.
An irregular highlighted gray mound with a darker foot still reads as a pebble at 2x.
The compact angular gray form retains a lit upper face and shaded base, reading as a pebble at 2x.
Two offset gray masses retain the paired-pebble silhouette even at 2x.
The diagonal tapered green silhouette and lighter central area still suggest a single leaf at 2x.
The source's lobed autumn-leaf outline and stem collapse into a short orange block; at 2x it no longer reads reliably as a leaf.
A white bloom with a warm center remains above a broad green pad, preserving the water-lily reading at 2x.
